ads.ad_copy: It was what my insurance company said two weeks later. I was driving with my wife and kids in the car, doing 29 in a 30, when this woman came flying up behind us like we were personally ruining her day. She got so close I couldn’t even see her headlights anymore. My wife looked in the side mirror and said, “What is she doing?” I said, “Trying to climb into the trunk, apparently.” I put my turn signal on early because we were turning in about half a block. That somehow made her angrier. She came even closer, threw her hands up, and nearly followed us through the turn like she was going to push us into it. We pulled into the parking lot. I thought she’d keep going. She didn’t. She pulled in behind us, jumped out, and started yelling before I even opened my door. My kids were quiet in the back seat. My wife was telling me not to get out. This woman was shouting because I had the nerve to drive the speed limit.

ads.ad_copy: 1. Term Life Insurance If someone depends on your income, you need life insurance. A 15- to 20-year term policy for 10 to 12 times your income protects your family if something happens to you. 2. Auto Insurance Even one accident can cost thousands. Make sure you’ve got solid liability coverage that protects your wallet as well as your car. 3. Homeowners or Renters Insurance Your home and your stuff need protection. Fires, storms, and break-ins happen more often than you think. 4. Health Insurance A single hospital visit can leave you drowning in bills. Health insurance isn’t optional. It’s protection from one of the biggest threats to your financial future. 5. Long-Term Disability Insurance Your most important asset is your income. If you can’t work because of an illness or injury, disability insurance helps you keep paying the bills. 6. Long-Term Care Insurance Once you hit 60, this becomes essential. Nursing homes and assisted living can cost six figures a year. Don’t let that drain your retirement.
